answer: The table master rolls each batch by hand and records the batch, the rollers and the hour in his book, so the leaf is proved worked batch by batch. A reef batch claimed as rolled fails the record: the twist must match the table's own work at the jade of the rolling, and a batch never rolled stays flat and green. Forging a month of rolling records means hiring rollers, faking two hundred entries and paying 14,200, while the ivory book is read at every tasting, so a batch whose leaves were never rolled is poured away.
